items.text: A powerful Thanksgiving storm is expected to bring heavy rain, damaging winds and coastal flooding to the East Coast Wednesday and Thursday, the National Weather Service says.
items.detail: The Weather Prediction Center said Monday that "confidence is high for an impactful holiday storm" from Wednesday through Saturday. The heaviest rain is expected on Thanksgiving Day along the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast coasts: 1 to 4 inches in the Carolinas and Mid-Atlantic and 1 to 2 inches in the Northeast, with a risk of flooding rain from the Virginia Tidewater to southern New England. Gusts of 50+ mph are forecast along the coast and 40+ mph inland along the I-95 corridor, with power outages and downed trees possible. High surf and high tides could bring significant coastal flooding and beach erosion from Georgia to the Northeast, and snow showers are possible Friday into Saturday. Forecasters urged travelers to monitor forecasts.
items.why: It lands on one of the busiest travel days of the year in the most crowded part of the country.

items.text: The death toll from Sunday's Russian drone strike on an apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv, rose to 11, regional officials said Monday.
items.detail: Kyiv regional military administration head Tymur Tkachenko said rescuers recovered another body from the rubble; Sunday evening's count was four. Emergency crews worked through the night, pausing only for air-raid alerts, and pulled a 7-year-old boy alive after 14 hours under the debris, the State Emergency Service said. Three more people were killed Sunday when a drone hit a supermarket in Vyshneve.
items.why: The toll nearly tripled overnight, making it one of the deadliest strikes near Kyiv in weeks.

items.text: Russia's corvette Merkury, one of its newest warships, was sunk by Ukrainian sea drones at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Monday.
items.detail: Zelenskiy said seven Ukrainian-made naval drones were used near the Libyan coast and also hit a second target, the Russian cargo ship MV Angara, which he said Russia used to carry weapons; a Russian Ka-27 helicopter was destroyed with the corvette, which entered service in 2023. "We continue operations in designated waters," he said on Telegram. Libya's eastern government reported an explosion and fire on a Russian ship at the Benghazi naval base early Sunday and opened a joint investigation with Russia. Russia had not commented.
items.why: Ukraine is now striking Russian forces far from the war zone, on a third country's soil.

items.text: The Army plans to blow up nearly five tons of unstable explosive material at an Iowa ammunition plant Wednesday despite a court pause, and the Justice Department asked judges Sunday to lift it.
items.detail: A federal appeals court on Thursday paused an EPA permit for destroying nearly 70 drums of lead azide, a compound used to set off munitions, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, after environmental groups sued over a possible lead-dust plume over Iowa, the Mississippi River and parts of Illinois. In a filing late Saturday the Justice Department said the order does not stop the Army from acting under a separate legal authority, arguing the material could explode on its own as temperatures drop. The Army moved the detonation to Wednesday for better weather; Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds activated the state emergency operations center and the FAA restricted flights over the area through Wednesday.
items.why: It tests whether the military can go ahead with a risky operation while a court has it on hold.

items.text: U.S. stock futures jumped Monday after last week's AI-driven rout, while South Korea, Taiwan and China moved to steady their own sliding markets.
items.detail: Nasdaq 100 futures rose 3.3% and S&P 500 futures 2.5% by 3:51 a.m. ET, Reuters reported, after the Nasdaq's 10% drop last week, its worst since March 2020. South Korea's KOSPI, now half its peak, still fell about 3.3% as the finance minister repeated plans to stabilize the market if needed; Taiwan's regulator tightened short-selling rules and Taiwan stocks rose 2.1%; Chinese exchanges eased margin-financing rules. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.96% and gold gained 2.1%. Dell reports Tuesday.
items.why: Futures point to a rebound, but governments abroad are stepping in to stop the slide.

items.text: House Democrats reached at least 258 seats Sunday, their largest majority since 1992, after Rep. Virginia Foxx conceded her North Carolina race following a recount.
items.detail: Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a longtime local newspaper journalist, defeated Foxx, the 11-term chair of the House Rules Committee, by about 330 votes out of roughly 287,000 cast in North Carolina's 5th District; the AP called the race Sunday afternoon after the recount. The 258 seats top the 257 Democrats won in 2008 and match their 1992 total; a few races are still uncalled. With the Senate also in Democratic hands, Hakeem Jeffries is on track to become the first Black House speaker in January, facing a Republican president who has vowed to veto Democratic bills.
items.why: A majority this large lets House Democrats pass bills and run oversight of the Trump administration without relying on a handful of swing votes.

items.text: All three objects that crashed in Poland on Friday were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles, Polish prosecutors said Sunday, not two missiles and a drone as first reported.
items.detail: The Lublin regional prosecutor's office said wreckage at Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem and Mołodycz in southeastern Poland all came from Kh-101s, which preliminary findings show were built in the fourth quarter of 2026 in Dubna, near Moscow; lab tests are not finished. Work at Mołodycz resumes Monday. NATO's North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels Monday to discuss the incursions. No one was hurt; Russia has not commented.
items.why: Three Russian cruise missiles landing on NATO soil is a more serious breach than first thought and raises pressure for an alliance response.

items.text: The UN's COP31 climate talks in Turkey collapsed Sunday without a final agreement after the European Union and others rejected a deal that did not mention fossil fuels.
items.detail: Summit president Murat Kurum, Turkey's environment minister, told the closing session in Antalya that the main decisions were not adopted for lack of consensus. Ireland's climate minister, speaking for the EU, said the bloc would not endorse an "Antalya Pact" that does not even mention fossil fuels; an earlier draft had called for a faster phase-out before later versions dropped the language. UN Secretary-General António Guterres said he was "deeply disappointed." The summit ran two days past its scheduled end, the longest UN climate conference on record.
items.why: It is a rare outright failure of the yearly UN climate process, leaving no new global commitments on cutting fossil fuel use.

items.text: Delta Air Lines flights were delayed nationwide Sunday after its weight-and-balance computer system failed, forcing an FAA ground stop at Atlanta days before Thanksgiving.
items.detail: The FAA said the problem was with Delta's automated system for calculating aircraft weight and balance, not air traffic control; it issued a ground stop and then a ground delay at Hartsfield-Jackson at Delta's request. Delta used manual workarounds and said Sunday afternoon the system was working again. About 1,650 Delta flights, roughly half the day's schedule, were delayed by 4 p.m. ET, about 70% of them from the outage, but only a few dozen were canceled. Separately, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said Sunday Americans should expect more technology outages as companies and agencies replace aging systems.
items.why: It snarled one of the biggest U.S. airlines at the start of the busiest travel week of the year, after a string of bank, FAA and government system failures.

also.text: Carlos Alcaraz won his first ATP Finals title Sunday in Turin, beating world No. 1 Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6.
also.detail: The 23-year-old Spaniard saved three straight set points in the second-set tiebreaker and went 5-0 for the week, earning a record $5.17 million. He joins Andre Agassi, Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic as the only men to win all four majors and the season-ending championships. Zverev stays No. 1.
also.why: It caps a comeback season for tennis's biggest star after a four-month injury layoff.

also.text: Nvidia must explain its chip sales to China and who handled compliance, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday on CBS's "Face the Nation."
also.detail: Bessent said the administration has been in touch with Nvidia's interim management, lead directors and lawyers: "We do need to see who was in charge of compliance there... Did it go all the way to the top?" Asked about President Trump's call for ousted CEO Jensen Huang to apologize and return, Bessent said, "we have to see where the buck stops." Nvidia's board chairman has said the board will not rehire Huang, who resigned after reports of an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence suspects is a Chinese spy.
also.why: It signals the administration's scrutiny of the world's top AI chipmaker is widening from Huang to the company's export controls.
